title: Cesaro telescoping gives EB approximation in a faithful KMS metric without normality

statement.quantifiers: Every finite faithful stationary self-compatible UCP T; integer N>=1. Separately, reversible or KMS-normal T for pointwise-power statements.
statement.assertion: For F_N=N^-1sum T^k and ONE C8 comparator Psi, Lambda_N=Psi F_N is EB with weighted L2 error<=4/sqrtN; source also supplies reversible sqrt(2n^n/(n+1)^(n+1)) and normal2sqrt(n^n/(n+1)^(n+1)) pointwise-power bounds.
assumptions: KMS contraction and positive selfadjoint comparator.
Pointwise spectral calculus requires reversible/normal hypotheses; arbitrary case is Cesaro here.

inputs: Original channel, one common comparator and finite iteration count.
interface.precision: Finite exact inequalities; no spectral gap assumption.
costs: Measurement/acquisition costs and weighted inverse conditioning separate from analytic bound.
Earlier tracial nonnormal pointwise insertion-average theorem remains distinct.

proof_mechanism: Comparator displacement square bounded by its Dirichlet form.
Reversible powers use scalar spectral maximum x^n(1-x).
KMS contraction and Cauchy-Schwarz give energy<=2||A||^2/N, hence C8 squared error<=16||A||^2/N.
